# Why does H2O filter motions with a privileged policy, and does RGB alone close the robot loop?

> **Current answer:** H2O's sim-to-data filter uses a privileged motion imitator to reject retargeted motions that are difficult to execute under robot dynamics, and the paper's ablation supports improved deployment-policy success. However, RGB-only describes the human command input: robot linear velocity on hardware still comes from external motion capture, so the complete loop is not localization-free.
